encounter_rewrites.title: Act II: Crinan's Rising
encounter_rewrites.body: The uprising is deeply personal, dynastic, and remarkably short-lived in its impact on the wider realm. It proves that the old king's family still has political reach, yet lacks sufficient force to dislodge Macbeth once the new regime has fully hardened around him with iron resolve and military backing from the south. This brief conflict serves as a warning rather than a threat, cementing the transition of power while acknowledging the lingering shadows of the past dynasty within the court's memory.
reaction_rewrites: The rebellion dies fast enough to remind the court that Macbeth is not merely holding the throne; he is willing to defend it. The next claim will remember it. In Alba, the record outlives the moment.
Mercy might quiet one feud, but it also tells every claimant that the kingdom can be tested. The next claim will remember it. In Alba, the record outlives the moment.

The king's defenders now have a cleaner story to tell: Macbeth is the ruler who kept Alba intact when the old house fractured. The next claim will remember it. In Alba, the record outlives the moment.
